- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially if recent price is rising.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction to next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa), model often lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 1–2 days.
- If model shows strong upward trend but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), reduce forecast slope or introduce early reversal signal.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may overreact; reduce forecast magnitude or add volatility dampening factor.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; consider smoothing or using rolling average of recent 7–14 days for baseline.
